rationale:
Evidence. The iteration 4 candidate (sensor spread x = -0.03..+0.03, size 0.012) scored 133.9, below the iteration 1 design at 154.1. Line loss did not fall: 1.25 per run on the oval, 1.15 on the s-bend and 1.05 on the slalom. So the narrower spread hurt tracking and did not address line loss. Across iterations 1 to 4 line loss has stayed at about 1.0 per run whatever the spread, footprint or kp, and every run except two ended off_track. Steering oscillation of 0.11 to 0.30 shows the controller is under-correcting, not unstable. Iteration 2 showed that raising kp to 3.5 alone lowered the score, so kp is not the lever. Iteration 1 (spread ±0.04) remains the best raced geometry.

Change. I return geometry.sensor_positions to x = -0.04, -0.02, 0.0, 0.02, 0.04 at y = 0.03, with sensor_size 0.012, as the Evaluator's first requested change asks. I also lower controller.kd from 0.5 to 0.35, the middle of the 0.3 to 0.4 range the Evaluator suggested. kp 3.0, ki 0.05, base_speed 1.4, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] and line_loss last_direction are unchanged from iteration 1. This makes kd the only variable changed from the best raced design, so its effect can be read cleanly.

Hypotheses. (a) Line loss is driven by turn-in lag: with kd 0.5 the controller over-damps the signal change at the bend entry, so the tape slips out of the sensors. Lower kd should reduce line-loss events toward 0.9 or below on the s-bend and slalom. (b) If kd has little effect on line loss, the cause is in the control response itself, not in the geometry or damping, and the next test should be a forward sensor offset (y greater than 0.03) to give earlier sight of the tape.

Expected result. A score at or above about 154, with s-bend and slalom progress at least as high as iteration 1. Risk: lower kd may raise steering oscillation on the oval above 0.3. If so, the next step is to restore kd to 0.5 and test base_speed or a forward sensor offset, rather than raising kp again.

Measurements wanted: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and noise_robustness on each track, so that the kd effect can be separated from speed and geometry.
